questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following as used in economics:

(i) Debentures

(ii) Plough-back profit

(iii) Deregulation

(iv) Parastatals

(v) Multinational

(vi) Shares

(2+2+2+2+2+2 = 12 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Each correct definition earns 2 marks.

**(i) Debentures.** Long-term **loan certificates** issued by a company to borrow money from the public. The holder is a **creditor, not an owner**: he receives a **fixed rate of interest** whether the company makes a profit or not, and the loan is repaid on a stated date. Interest is paid before any dividend to shareholders.

**(ii) Plough-back profit (retained profit).** The part of a firm's **net profit that is not shared out** to the owners but is **kept in the business and reinvested** to buy new machines, expand or increase working capital. It is an **internal source of finance**.

**(iii) Deregulation.** The **removal or reduction of government rules and controls** over an industry or market (for example licences, price controls or monopoly rights) so that more firms can enter and competition increases. It is often linked with liberalisation and privatisation.

**(iv) Parastatals.** **Public enterprises**: firms or corporations **owned and controlled wholly or partly by the government** and set up to provide goods and services, such as electricity, water, transport or postal services.

**(v) Multinational (company).** A firm that **owns and controls production or business activities in two or more countries**, with its headquarters in one country and branches or subsidiaries abroad. It is usually very large and brings capital and technology.

**(vi) Shares.** The **units into which the capital of a joint-stock (limited) company is divided**. A person who buys shares becomes a **part-owner (shareholder)** of the company, has the right to vote (ordinary shares) and receives a share of profit called a **dividend**, which varies with the profit made.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Bring out any Four (04) reasons why about 60% of entrepreneurs started as Sole Proprietors?

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** A **sole proprietorship** (sole trader) is a business **owned, financed and managed by one person**. Many entrepreneurs begin as sole proprietors for the following reasons.

1. **Easy and cheap to set up (2 marks).** There are **few legal formalities**: no complicated registration or agreement is needed, so a person can start quickly, for example a trader opening a small shop or a tailor opening a workshop.
2. **Small capital is enough (2 marks).** The owner can start with **personal savings** or a small loan from family and friends. No large sum is needed to begin.
3. **Owner keeps all the profit and has full control (2 marks).** There are **no partners or shareholders** to share the profit with, and the owner takes **quick decisions** without consulting anyone. This is a strong incentive.
4. **Personal contact, flexibility and secrecy (2 marks).** The owner knows his customers personally and can adapt to their needs. Business affairs are **kept private** because the accounts need not be published.

*Other acceptable reasons:* the business is easy to close, taxes and regulations are light, and the owner has the satisfaction of being his own boss.

**Conclusion.** Because it is easy, cheap and gives full control and profit to the owner, the sole proprietorship is the usual starting point for entrepreneurs, even though it has unlimited liability and limited capital.
